audience: An assistant with no prior context on this codebase. Follow steps in order. Do not skip verification.
summary: A full-screen hero whose background is a video played frame by frame, scrubbed by scroll position. The frames are pre-extracted still images drawn onto a canvas, not a video element.

hardRules.rule: Never delete, rename or rewrite anything you did not create in this task.
hardRules.why: You are adding to a working system. Every existing feature must behave identically when you finish.
forbidden: changing a router or the ids and classes it depends on
reformatting or tidying code you were not asked to touch
hardRules.preferredAlternative: Create a new file. Adding is almost always safer than editing.

hardRules.rule: Verify after every step, not at the end.
hardRules.why: Six small verified steps localise a failure to one step. One large unverified change does not.
Every number in this spec came from measurement. 'It should be fine' is how bottlenecks ship.

hardRules.rule: If the feature cannot be added without removing an existing one, stop and report.
hardRules.why: A hero that broke the export button is worse than no hero.

mechanism: A tall section creates scroll distance.
A sticky child stays pinned while that distance passes.
Scroll position through the tall section becomes progress from 0 to 1.
concept.whyCanvasNotVideoTag: A video element cannot be scrubbed smoothly. Setting currentTime forces a seek and decode from the nearest keyframe, which stutters under fast scrolling. Pre-extracted stills have no seek cost.
concept.whyCanvasNotImgSrcSwap: Swapping an img src causes a decode and layout flash per frame. Drawing an already-decoded Image onto a canvas is one blit. Decode once, draw many.

count.reason: Enough for smooth motion without excessive weight.

constraints.constraint: Zero-pad the frame number to 3 digits.
constraints.why: Without padding, f10 sorts before f2 and the sequence plays out of order.

constraints.constraint: Sample evenly across the entire source clip.
constraints.why: Taking the first N frames of a long clip yields the opening moment in slow motion, not the clip.

verify.check: Files are sequential with no gaps from f001 to fNNN.
The first and last frame look like the start and end of the clip, not two frames a second apart.
Folder total is under the size budget.

steps.action: Extract frames from the source video, resize, compress, and name them per inputs.frames.

verify.expect: blank canvas is correct at this stage

steps.name: Add the CSS
creates: a new stylesheet, or an appended block

declarations.why: The scroll distance that plays the sequence. Roughly two and a half screens.
Pins the stage while the tall parent scrolls past.
declarations.warning: Any overflow:hidden on an ancestor silently disables sticky. This is the most common cause of 'sticky does not work'.

declarations.why: Lets you draw at the frame's natural size and let CSS crop to the viewport, so no draw-rectangle recalculation on resize.
The frames are a backdrop. At full opacity the text is unreadable.
Makes text legible over a bright frame.
declarations.warning: Must be pointer-events:none or it swallows clicks.

declarations.why: Content must sit above both the canvas and the gradient.

verify.check: The headline stays pinned mid-screen for a while, then releases.

steps.name: Write the scroll logic
steps.warning: Write this in a NEW file. Do not append to an existing script.

criticalLines.why: Scroll fires far more often than the screen refreshes. This collapses a burst into one draw per animation frame.
Tells the browser you will not call preventDefault, so it need not wait for your handler before scrolling.
Most scroll events land on the same frame index. Redrawing an identical image is pure waste.
Frames arrive out of order relative to scrolling. Never show a blank canvas.
A hidden hero returns zeroes, progress becomes NaN, and the frame index is poisoned. See pitfall P7.
One missing frame must not stall the whole sequence.

verify.check: Scrolling plays the sequence forward and backward.

steps.name: Add progressive loading

rationale.doNotAwaitAll: On a slow connection that is several seconds of blank hero.
rationale.concurrencyChoice: One at a time wastes the connection. All at once floods it and the browser queues them anyway. Six keeps the pipe full without starving fonts, stylesheets and content.

verify.expect: First frame appears almost at once; scrubbing never shows a blank canvas, only a slightly stale frame.

steps.name: Wire the script in
modifies: the page's HTML, by insertion only
steps.action: Add <script src="js/hero.js"></script> at the end of <body>, after the markup and after any script it depends on.
warnings: Do not place it in <head> without defer.
Do not mix defer with reliance on document order.

verify.onFail: 'Cannot read properties of null' means the script ran before the markup existed.

pitfalls.symptom: A file edit appears to succeed but the file is unchanged.
pitfalls.cause: Writing file content through a shell heredoc. Quotes, apostrophes and backticks break the shell parser and the command silently does nothing.
pitfalls.fix: Write files with a file-writing tool, not by piping text through a shell. If unavoidable, verify the file actually changed afterwards.
pitfalls.realCost: Two fixes were applied to a file that had never been written.

pitfalls.symptom: Staggered entrance animations do not stagger; children appear all at once or not at all.
pitfalls.cause: A wrapper element carries its own fade while its children carry theirs. Nested opacity multiplies, so a child at 0ms inside a parent at 170ms stays invisible until the parent catches up.
pitfalls.fix: Only leaf elements carry an entrance animation. Never nest a staged child inside a staged parent.

pitfalls.symptom: A drop or click lands at the wrong position, off by exactly the scroll distance.
pitfalls.cause: Adding container.scrollLeft to a coordinate derived from getBoundingClientRect, which already accounts for scroll.
pitfalls.fix: Rect coordinates are viewport-relative. Do not add scroll to them.

pitfalls.cause: Pinned to the bottom of the sticky stage, directly inside the darkest part of the overlay gradient.
pitfalls.fix: Place the cue in the content flow beneath the buttons, where the gradient is not at its strongest.

pitfalls.symptom: A button renders as bare underlined text after being changed to a link.
pitfalls.cause: The styling was attached to the 'button' element selector, which an anchor does not inherit.
pitfalls.fix: When you change an element's tag, re-check every style that targeted the old tag.

pitfalls.symptom: The hero plays the opening moment of the clip in slow motion.
pitfalls.cause: Taking the first N frames of a long source instead of sampling across it.
pitfalls.fix: Use the even-sampling formula in inputs.frames.constraints.I2.

pitfalls.symptom: Frame index becomes NaN; canvas stops updating.
pitfalls.cause: A hidden hero still receives scroll events. getBoundingClientRect returns zeroes and the progress division produces NaN.
pitfalls.fix: Guard on rect.height === 0 before computing anything.

performance.measured: 300 frames at full size was 35 MB. 80 frames at 900x506 quality 64 was 3.8 MB and looks the same in motion.
performance.action: Measure the folder. Above 5 MB, cut frames or quality.

performance.rule: Never decode inside the scroll handler.
performance.bad: setting img.src or constructing an Image during scroll
performance.good: load each frame once into an array, then only ever drawImage

performance.why: Scroll can fire over 100 times a second against 60 screen refreshes.
Assigning canvas.width or canvas.height clears and reallocates the entire canvas, even when assigning the value it already holds.

performance.rule: Do not interleave layout reads and style writes.
performance.good: read everything first, then write everything

performance.rule: Do not block the first paint.
performance.good: draw frame one, then load the rest in the background

performance.rule: Revoke any object URLs you create.
performance.why: Otherwise tab memory grows on every reload.

rollback.before: Ensure the working tree is committed and clean before starting.

commands.use: must be clean before you begin
review what you changed before committing
park everything and return to known-good

rollback.policy: If a change breaks an unrelated feature, revert rather than patch around it. Understand the cause, then reapply properly. A workaround stacked on a misunderstanding is how a codebase rots.

acceptance.check: Frame folder is zero-padded, sequential and evenly sampled.
Total frame weight is under 5 MB.
Canvas dimensions are set once, not per draw.
Scroll handler is passive and coalesced with requestAnimationFrame.
First frame paints before the rest have loaded.
Scrubbing never shows a blank canvas.
Text is legible over the brightest frame in the sequence.

acceptance.note: This is the check people skip. It is the one that catches you having broken something else.

acceptance.check: Console is clean and the network tab shows exactly frameCount image requests, all 200.
Work is committed with a message saying what changed and why.

closingNote: The hardest part of this task is not the animation. It is finishing it without damaging anything around it. You will be tempted to reformat a file you are passing through, rename something for clarity, or delete a line that looks unused. Resist all of it. The line that looks unused is load-bearing about a third of the time, and you will not find out until later. Add, verify, and leave the rest alone.
